dedupe_keys.name: geomatchd conceptual design tool for geothermal district heating and cooling

description: Geomatchd is a software tool to help non-experts carry out rapid conceptual design of geothermal district heating systems that use local shallow geothermal resources. It was developed at the National Energy Technology Laboratory by Danylo Oryshchyn and colleagues with sponsorship from the DOE Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office. It has three parts: user-side heating and cooling demand profiles, district heating and cooling network models for sizing and optimal layout selection, and geothermal system models for heat extraction and cost comparison. The architecture is described as open source so that others can improve functions and reuse its code and data. The method is location-independent. It is distributed as downloadable ZIP resources of about 237 MB on NETL's Energy Data eXchange, created in August 2026, at no cost. Caveats: the EDX page states that no licence is specified, so reuse terms should be checked with the contact, and the page gives no programming language or system requirements. Simulation uses are early-stage sizing and optimisation of geothermal district heating and cooling networks. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
